column5: Anna chat interface on the home page
column6: The home page displays a chat interface with Anna (AI assistant). Users can ask free-text questions and receive answers with card layouts, streaming text simulation and suggestion chips for follow-up questions.
Anna generates a route-specific greeting and follow-up questions. The home page shows a daily briefing, detail pages show a summary of the current record.
Anna answers questions using keyword rules (no LLM). Answers can contain cards with structured data, danger/warning markers and clickable actions.
Anna detects danger and warning keywords in her responses and highlights affected passages in color (red for danger, yellow for warning).
All InterRAI assessments are displayed in a filterable list. Views: All, In Progress, Completed, Re-Assessment Due. Per entry: patient name, type, completion rate, assessor.
A workspace for item entry with sticky TOC navigation (left), collapsible section accordions and progressive disclosure (compact rows for high confidence, expanded for uncertain items).

Approx. 225 official InterRAI HC Switzerland items in sections A through S. Each item has a code, short question, full question, answer type (scale/yes-no/text/number) and answer options with short labels.
Completed assessments display all captured items, CAP results (Clinical Assessment Protocols) and outcome scales in a non-editable view.
An overlay shows outcome scales (ADL, IADL, CPS, DRS, PAIN etc.) with bar charts, triggered CAPs with priority and trigger items, and a section overview with completion status.
Editor for nursing diagnoses (NANDA codes), interventions and goals. Diagnoses as ReviewBlock cards with collapsible body (rationale, linked interventions/goals). Adding via NANDA catalog search.
Curated selection of 12 NANDA diagnoses with ENP-oriented intervention and SMART goal suggestions. When adding a diagnosis, the first intervention and first goal are automatically suggested.

column5: KLV prescription workspace with status pipeline
column6: A workspace for KLV prescriptions with a 7-step status pipeline: Draft → Reviewed → With Physician → Returned from Physician → With Insurance → Cost Approval Received / Rejected.
Complete service catalog with approx. 170 positions. Per position: catalog number, description, area, standard time in minutes, KLV category (a/b/c) and default frequency.
Calculation of hours/week per position and totals by category (a/b/c). Considers rhythm (daily/weekly/monthly/one-time/as needed), number of visits and simultaneous partners.
Automatic check whether a recorded KLV position is already included in another captured position (e.g. full body wash includes hair washing). Warning with main service reference.
Check of insurance-specific billing limits (e.g. Groupe Mutuel max. 6 days/week, KPT max. 60 min. initial assessment). Warning only, no compliance certification.

Per KLV position a justification draft for effectiveness, appropriateness and efficiency is generated. Three cases: justifiable (diagnosis linked), suggestion (Anna suggests a link), gap (no suitable diagnosis).
A globally persistent recording (survives tab switches) records a conversation. After stopping, mock artifacts are automatically generated: InterRAI items, nursing diagnoses, KLV positions.

A persistent bar at the top of the screen shows the recording status: red pulse dot with timer (recording), spinner (processing), green expandable summary with deep links to generated artifacts (result).

A realistic demo conversation between nurse and client with transcript segments. Each segment carries recognized InterRAI items, NANDA diagnosis suggestions and KLV suggestions for artifact generation.
Inclusive rules and insurance rules are defined as table-based arrays. New rules = new array element, no logic change needed. WZW mapping table similarly extensible.
The strategic dashboard shows an Anna daily briefing that adapts to the current role: nurse sees client focus, back office sees billing focus, management sees pipeline focus.
Three metric cards: Active Clients (with trend), Onboarding Pipeline (by status), Staff Status (active nurses with capacity).
Six workflow metrics as risk indicators: SRC course overdue, re-assessment due, residence permit B pending, withholding tax registration, child allowance application, salary adjustment after SRC.
All onboarding cases in a filterable list. Status: In Capture, Incomplete, Blocked. Per case: patient, caregiver, start date, responsible person, Anna context banner.
Guided wizard with steps: 1) Caregiver (HR data), 2) Patient (clinical data + documents), 3) Contract signing. For residence permit B an additional special permit step appears.

Capture of personal data, residence permit status (A-N), withholding tax data, partner data (conditional on marriage/WHT), children and allowances, employment data (hourly wage, IBAN), mandatory documents (ID, insurance card etc.).

Capture in 9 tabs: Personal data, Social & Tax, Medical history (falls/mood/medication), Activities (ADL with 22 items), InterRAI, Care Planning, KLV, Workflow, Documents (17 mandatory/optional documents).

column5: Compliance hard gate residence permit B
column6: Residence permit B triggers a mandatory submission of special permit confirmation from migration authority. The contract step is blocked until the confirmation is uploaded. A dynamic sidebar step appears.

column5: Compliance medium validation residence permit G
column6: Residence permit G (cross-border permit) generates a prominent warning with direct upload action for permit G document. No block, but visible action required.
Dependent children or child allowances through Spitex generate a neutral informational hint: family/birth certificate upload as mandatory document. No block.

Canvas-based signature pad for 4 documents (job description, employment contract, privacy policy, consent form). Signature with timestamp and signer name. Employment contract is hard gate for onboarding completion.

column5: Physician request domain object and flow
column6: A dedicated domain object (ArztAnfrage) models the entire physician contact flow: waiting for consent → ready to send → sent (with day counter and reminder) → response received → diagnoses extracted.

The prepared email to the physician has an editable subject and body (pre-filled from template with resolved placeholders). Fixed parts (attachment note, sender signature) are visible but not editable. Reset to template available.
After simulated physician response Anna extracts diagnoses from the attachment and presents them as drafts (status: suggestion) for manual review. No auto-acceptance — four-eyes principle.

Medical diagnoses (ICD codes) exist as a standalone artifact on the case with lead conversion IDs (onboardingId + patientId). Fields: ICD code, description, source (physician response or manually entered), status (draft/confirmed).
Medical diagnoses in care planning: drafts as compact rows with ochre accent and suggestion pill (confirm/reject), confirmed as quiet single-line reference. Manual entry as equivalent input path.

Nursing diagnoses carry an icdIds field referencing medical diagnoses. The justification chain reads: KLV service → nursing diagnosis (diagnoseIds) → medical diagnosis (icdIds). No direct KLV-to-ICD mapping.

column5: KLV tab shows medical diagnoses from artifact
column6: The KLV tab displays confirmed medical diagnoses from the shared artifact in the diagnosis header area. No copy — care planning and KLV read the same object.

The steps 'Physician contacted' and 'Diagnosis & medication list received' derive their completion status automatically from the ArztAnfrage object. Read-only checkboxes with automatic provenance and date.
The conversion creates active patient and caregiver records from an onboarding case. Clinical artifacts (InterRAI, care planning, KLV, workflows) receive the new patientId.
column9: Sets patientId on artifacts; full conversion logic is a stub

column6: Missing mandatory documents do not absolutely block completion. An override dialog lists missing documents by name and requires a mandatory justification. Employment contract remains a hard lock (no override).

column5: Case status header with aggregate pills
column6: The onboarding header shows a deterministic status (Draft / In Progress / Ready to Complete) and clickable pills: 'X of Y steps' (→ workflow tab), 'N documents open' (→ documents tab, ochre only as last blocker).
Prioritized hint line: 1) Physician response received → jump to care planning, 2) Request ready to send → jump, 3) unconfirmed suggestions. Collapses on scroll. No display when no action needed.
The conversation recording button sits right-aligned in the patient step tab bar. Three states: ready (Anna gradient), active (pulse dot + 'Stop'), busy (disabled). Tabs scroll, button stays fixed.
Physician request sending requires explicit confirmation with visible recipient. No auto-send to potentially outdated physician contact (privacy risk). Documented as code comment.
Workflow step derivations (SCHRITT_ABLEITUNGEN) are defined as an array structure. New binding = new object with stepLabel, isCompleted function and provenance function. No logic change needed.
A single abschlussPruefung function provides employmentContractOk, missingMandatoryDocuments and complete. Header status, footer lock and completion dialog all use the same derivation.
Compliance gates in three tiers: Hard Gate (blocks contract, e.g. permit B), Medium Validation (prominent hint with action, e.g. permit G), Soft Validation (informational, e.g. child allowances).
Patients are displayed in a table with views (All, Mine, Attention). Per row: name, severity pill, status, assigned nurse, next task. Search and sorting.
Patient detail page with 7 tabs: Overview (master data, Anna summary), Medical History, Care Planning (NANDA), KLV (services), Documents, Workflow/Process, Activities (ADL).
Patient status (Active, Paused, Ended) can be changed via a modal with confirmation dialog. Status change updates the display in both list and detail views.
Anna generates a structured summary in the overview tab from master data: age, severity, care level, assigned nurse, open tasks, current diagnoses.
AHV number, IBAN and other identification numbers are masked by default (e.g. 756.****.****.XX). A reveal icon allows deliberate unmasking. Reveals are in principle auditable.
The documents tab shows a SharePoint-like folder structure (8 categories). Per document: upload (file/camera), preview, delete. Progress display for mandatory documents.
Caregivers in a table with 5 views: All, Mine, Attention, SRC open, In Onboarding. Per row: name, HR status checks, SRC progress, stamp warnings, assigned patients.
Detail page with tabs: Overview (master data, HR checks), Personal/HR (employment, withholding tax), Family/Tax (partner, children, allowances), Bank Details (IBAN, masked), Documents, Monthly Steps.
HR checks (SRC course status, withholding tax registration, residence permit document) are shown as colored status indicators: green (completed), yellow (pending), red (overdue).
When the SRC care course is not completed within one year of contract signing, services are paused. The warning shows remaining time and affected patients.
AHV number, ZEMIS number and IBAN are displayed masked. Reveal via deliberate click on the eye icon.
Weighted matching: language (40%), professional skills (25%), region/distance (20%), available capacity (15%). Calculates a percentage score per candidate.
The three best matches are shown with total score, criteria breakdown (bar per dimension) and contact details. Allocation confirmable via click.
A slide-over sidebar opens directly from the patient list showing match suggestions for the selected patient. Allocation without page change.
Workflow tasks (automatically generated) and service tickets (manually created) are combined in a unified view. Consistent display with type icons and due date colors.
Tasks are grouped by urgency: Overdue (red), Today (warning), This Week (neutral), Later (muted). Counter per bucket.
Each of the 15 types (SRC registration, re-assessment, permit B etc.) has its own Anna configuration: contextual explanation, specific action buttons, priority classification.
Anna shows a suggestion panel per opened task with contextual info and action buttons: open URL, copy data, download document, open email, execute demo mock.
Standalone section for management role: KPI aggregates (open/overdue tasks), staff workload (top 5 by task load), critical cases requiring action.
Responsive app shell: desktop sidebar (56px icon bar with tooltips and badges), mobile drawer, topbar (search, notifications, user menu), GlobalRecordingBar, Anna float button.
Search field in the topbar with instant results display. Searches across patients, caregivers and tasks. Results as clickable entries with type icon.
